newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down on Thursday despite two new listings on the Shenzhen stock market, traders said.
The most active seven-day contract fell to 12.69 percent from 16 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose to 5.99 million lots from 5.42 million on Wednesday.
"After active trading on Tuesday, there were fewer buyers today and that led to the fall," said one trader.
The listing on Friday of another three companies on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges was likely to prevent any further losses on Friday, another trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up after a technical correction early this week, traders said.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.74 million lots from 1.43 million on Wednesday.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 edged up to 116.80 yuan from Wednesday's 116.65 yuan.
"I think the spots will rise further in the next few days because of the high yield rates of many contracts," one trader said.

Some long-term investors had continued to buy on the market over the past few days, traders said, adding that the higher turnover was an indication that more buyers had entered the market on Thursday.
